text: For Azure SQL Database, Microsoft takes full, differential, and log backups automatically, on its own schedule. There's no BACKUP DATABASE statement here — there's simply nothing for you to configure.

Full backups happen roughly weekly, differentials every 12 to 24 hours, and log backups every 5 to 10 minutes — all triggered by Azure, and stored using the same redundancy option you already picked for the database.

Worth stating plainly: you lose direct visibility into backup jobs succeeding or failing, which is real on-prem DBA work. What you keep is the retention window, an optional long-term retention policy, and the redundancy tier.
That retention window is exactly where point-in-time restore comes in next, including the specific case of restoring a database that was deleted entirely.
